How much the **public BrainGlobe atlas data** is being downloaded, derived from
the S3 server access logs of the atlas bucket. Only successful object
downloads (`REST.GET.OBJECT`, HTTP 200/206) are counted. Totals are
cumulative since logging began and grow a little every day.

Each atlas is served as several resources — an annotation volume, one or more
reference/template images, a terminology, a packaged download, neuroglancer
state — under separate key namespaces. Only the annotation keys carry the
canonical atlas name, so the **per-atlas table and charts below count
annotation-set downloads**; the other resource types are summarised together
under "by resource type".

The atlas, country and client-tool breakdowns are stored as three independent
tables (`atlas_usage.parquet`, `atlas_usage_by_country.parquet`,
`atlas_usage_by_tool.parquet`), so there is no per-atlas country or tool
split — the country and tool figures cover all downloads.

The **client tool** is inferred from each request's `Referer` and
`User-Agent`: the browser viewers (neuroglancer, Pinpoint) set a recognisable
`Referer`; library/CLI clients are told apart by `User-Agent`, with
`aiobotocore`/`botocore` (i.e. `s3fs` + `zarr`) attributed to
`brainglobe-atlasapi`.

```{python}
# | label: load
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path
import json

import matplotlib as mpl
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

from oss_dashboard.atlas_logs.atlas_names import display_name
from oss_dashboard.atlas_logs.constants import (
    ATLAS_PARQUET_PATH,
    COUNTRY_PARQUET_PATH,
    STATE_PATH,
    TOOL_PARQUET_PATH,
)

GREEN = "#03A062"
BLUE = "#4178f3"
ORANGE = "#EE9040"
# A mid grey that stays legible on both the light and dark site themes.
INK = "#888888"

mpl.rcParams.update({
    "figure.facecolor": "none",
    "axes.facecolor": "none",
    "savefig.facecolor": "none",
    "savefig.transparent": True,
    "text.color": INK,
    "axes.labelcolor": INK,
    "axes.edgecolor": INK,
    "xtick.color": INK,
    "ytick.color": INK,
    "axes.titlecolor": INK,
    "axes.spines.top": False,
    "axes.spines.right": False,
    "font.size": 11,
})

GB = 1e9
TB = 1e12

def _read(path, columns):
    if path.exists():
        return pd.read_parquet(path)
    return pd.DataFrame(columns=columns)


usage = _read(
    ATLAS_PARQUET_PATH,
    ["date", "atlas", "resource", "requests", "bytes_sent"],
)
countries = _read(
    COUNTRY_PARQUET_PATH, ["date", "country", "requests", "bytes_sent"]
)
tools = _read(
    TOOL_PARQUET_PATH, ["date", "tool", "requests", "bytes_sent"]
)
has_data = not usage.empty

state = json.loads(STATE_PATH.read_text()) if STATE_PATH.exists() else {}
updated_at = state.get("updated_at")
```

```{python}
# | label: no-data
# | output: asis
if not has_data:
    print(
        "::: callout-note\n"
        "No atlas usage data has been collected yet. Run "
        "`python -m oss_dashboard.atlas_logs` to populate "
        "`oss_dashboard/data/atlas_usage.parquet`.\n:::"
    )
```

```{python}
# | label: derived
if has_data:
    usage["date"] = pd.to_datetime(usage["date"])

    # The per-atlas views use annotation-set downloads only (see intro).
    annotations = usage[usage["resource"] == "annotation"]

    by_atlas = (
        annotations.groupby("atlas")
        .agg(
            downloads=("requests", "sum"),
            gb=("bytes_sent", lambda s: s.sum() / GB),
        )
        .sort_values("downloads", ascending=False)
    )
    # Human-readable name for display; the index stays the raw key derived
    # by classify_key (used to filter "unclassified" etc).
    by_atlas["name"] = [display_name(atlas) for atlas in by_atlas.index]

    by_country = (
        countries.groupby("country")["requests"]
        .sum()
        .sort_values(ascending=False)
    )
    by_resource = (
        usage.groupby("resource")["requests"].sum().sort_values(ascending=False)
    )
    by_tool = (
        tools.groupby("tool")["requests"].sum().sort_values(ascending=False)
    )
    tool_gb = tools.groupby("tool")["bytes_sent"].sum() / GB
    by_day = (
        usage.groupby("date")
        .agg(downloads=("requests", "sum"), bytes_sent=("bytes_sent", "sum"))
        .asfreq("D", fill_value=0)
    )
    if not tools.empty:
        tools["date"] = pd.to_datetime(tools["date"])
        tool_daily = (
            tools.pivot_table(
                index="date",
                columns="tool",
                values="requests",
                aggfunc="sum",
                fill_value=0,
            )
            .asfreq("D", fill_value=0)
            .reindex(columns=by_tool.index)
        )
    else:
        tool_daily = pd.DataFrame()

    total_downloads = int(usage["requests"].sum())
    total_bytes = int(usage["bytes_sent"].sum())
    annotation_downloads = int(annotations["requests"].sum())
    n_atlases = int((by_atlas.index != "unclassified").sum())
    n_countries = int((by_country.index != "??").sum())
    span = f"{by_day.index.min():%d %b %Y} – {by_day.index.max():%d %b %Y}"
    n_days = by_day.shape[0]
```

```{python}
# | label: stat-cards
# | output: asis
if has_data:
    cards = [
        ("Downloads", f"{total_downloads:,}"),
        ("Data served", f"{total_bytes / TB:.2f} TB"),
        ("Atlases", f"{n_atlases}"),
        ("Annotation downloads", f"{annotation_downloads:,}"),
        ("Countries", f"{n_countries}"),
        ("Days covered", f"{n_days}"),
        ("Window", span),
    ]
    if not by_tool.empty:
        share = by_tool.iloc[0] / by_tool.sum() * 100
        cards.insert(
            4, ("Top client", f"{by_tool.index[0]} ({share:.0f}%)")
        )
    tiles = "".join(
        f'<div style="flex:1 1 8rem;border:1px solid {INK}55;border-radius:.5rem;'
        f'padding:.75rem 1rem">'
        f'<div style="font-size:.8rem;color:{INK}">{label}</div>'
        f'<div style="font-size:1.5rem;font-weight:600">{value}</div></div>'
        for label, value in cards
    )
    print(
        f'<div style="display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:.75rem;margin:1rem 0">'
        f"{tiles}</div>"
    )
    if updated_at:
        stamp = datetime.fromisoformat(updated_at).strftime(
            "%A, %d %B %Y %H:%M UTC"
        )
        print(f"\n*Data last updated: {stamp}*\n")
```

## Downloads by atlas

```{python}
# | label: table
if has_data:
    import itables

    table = by_atlas.reset_index()[["name", "downloads", "gb"]]
    table.columns = ["Atlas", "Downloads", "Data served (GB)"]
    table["Data served (GB)"] = table["Data served (GB)"].round(1)
    table["Share of downloads"] = (
        table["Downloads"] / annotation_downloads * 100
    ).round(1).astype(str) + "%"
    itables.show(
        table,
        classes="display nowrap cell-border",
        columnDefs=[{"className": "dt-left", "targets": "_all"}],
        order=[[1, "desc"]],
        paging=False,
        scrollX=True,
    )
```

```{python}
# | label: atlas-bars
# | fig-width: 9
# | fig-height: 7
if has_data:
    top = (
        by_atlas[by_atlas.index != "unclassified"]
        .head(15)
        .set_index("name")
    )
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 6))

    top["downloads"].sort_values().plot.barh(ax=axes[0], color=GREEN)
    axes[0].set_title("Downloads by atlas (top 15)")
    axes[0].set_xlabel("object downloads")
    axes[0].set_ylabel("")

    top["gb"].sort_values().plot.barh(ax=axes[1], color=BLUE)
    axes[1].set_title("Data served by atlas (top 15)")
    axes[1].set_xlabel("GB")
    axes[1].set_ylabel("")

    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
```

## Over time

```{python}
# | label: timeseries
# | fig-width: 9
# | fig-height: 6
if has_data:
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(10, 6), sharex=True)

    axes[0].plot(
        by_day.index, by_day["downloads"], color=GREEN, alpha=0.35, lw=1
    )
    axes[0].plot(
        by_day.index,
        by_day["downloads"].rolling(7, min_periods=1).mean(),
        color=GREEN,
        lw=2,
        label="7-day mean",
    )
    axes[0].set_ylabel("downloads / day")
    axes[0].legend(frameon=False)

    axes[1].fill_between(
        by_day.index, by_day["bytes_sent"] / GB, color=BLUE, alpha=0.5
    )
    axes[1].set_ylabel("GB served / day")

    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
```

## By country and resource

```{python}
# | label: country-resource
# | fig-width: 9
# | fig-height: 6
if has_data:
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 5))

    named = by_country[by_country.index != "??"].head(15)
    if not named.empty:
        named.sort_values().plot.barh(ax=axes[0], color=ORANGE)
    axes[0].set_title("Downloads by country (top 15)")
    axes[0].set_xlabel("object downloads")
    axes[0].set_ylabel("")

    by_resource.sort_values().plot.barh(ax=axes[1], color=GREEN)
    axes[1].set_title("Downloads by resource type")
    axes[1].set_xlabel("object downloads")
    axes[1].set_ylabel("")

    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

    country_total = int(by_country.sum())
    unresolved = int(by_country.get("??", 0))
    if unresolved and country_total:
        pct = unresolved / country_total * 100
        print(
            f"\n*{unresolved:,} downloads ({pct:.1f}%) came from IPs that "
            f"could not be resolved to a country.*"
        )
```

## By client tool

```{python}
# | label: tool-bars
# | fig-width: 9
# | fig-height: 4
if has_data and not by_tool.empty:
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4))

    by_tool.sort_values().plot.barh(ax=axes[0], color=GREEN)
    axes[0].set_title("Downloads by client tool")
    axes[0].set_xlabel("object downloads")
    axes[0].set_ylabel("")

    tool_gb.reindex(by_tool.index).sort_values().plot.barh(
        ax=axes[1], color=BLUE
    )
    axes[1].set_title("Data served by client tool")
    axes[1].set_xlabel("GB")
    axes[1].set_ylabel("")

    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
```

```{python}
# | label: tool-over-time
# | fig-width: 9
# | fig-height: 4
if has_data and not tool_daily.empty and tool_daily.shape[0] > 1:
    top = tool_daily[tool_daily.sum().sort_values(ascending=False).index[:6]]
    palette = [GREEN, BLUE, ORANGE, "#7B61FF", "#E0529C", INK]
    ax = top.plot.area(
        figsize=(10, 4), color=palette[: top.shape[1]], alpha=0.85, lw=0
    )
    ax.set_title("Downloads per day by client tool (top 6)")
    ax.set_xlabel("")
    ax.set_ylabel("downloads / day")
    ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=9, loc="upper left")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
```

```{python}
# | label: tool-table
# | output: asis
if has_data and not by_tool.empty:
    total = by_tool.sum()
    lines = ["| Client tool | Downloads | Share | Data served (GB) |",
             "| --- | --: | --: | --: |"]
    for name, downloads in by_tool.items():
        lines.append(
            f"| {name} | {downloads:,} | {downloads / total * 100:.1f}% "
            f"| {tool_gb.get(name, 0):,.1f} |"
        )
    print("\n".join(lines))
```
